bioPage.lead: Norwegian guitarist, singer and songwriter — rooted in blues-rock, built for the stage.

sections.title: Origins / Vardø
paragraphs: From the Arctic town of Vardø in Finnmark, Håvard Pedersen grew up with music as a driving force — expressive guitar tone, strong songs, and a commitment to playing live without shortcuts.
Today based between Vardø and Oslo, he brings northern identity and international blues-rock energy to clubs, festivals and concert halls across Norway and beyond.
sections.imageAlt: Håvard Pedersen — black and white press portrait

sections.title: Musical influences
paragraphs: Håvard's playing draws on classic blues-rock — Gary Moore, Stevie Ray Vaughan, Thin Lizzy, Jimi Hendrix and the wider British and American rock tradition — filtered through his own songwriting and live attack.
On stage the focus is guitar-driven power trio energy: riffs, dynamics, and songs that leave room for improvisation within a tight live band.

sections.title: Career
paragraphs: Håvard Pedersen has released albums and singles across more than a decade of recording and touring, from the debut Never Felt So Good (2011) through You and I (2021) and recent singles including Det sku bli oss (2025).
He fronts Håvard Pedersen & The Blues Is Alright Band for full-band shows, and in 2026 leads the Håvard Pedersen Trio — a lean power trio format with Wild Willy Bendiksen and Knut Evenmo.

sections.title: Releases
paragraphs: Albums: Never Felt So Good (2011), You and I (2021). Singles and catalogue highlights include Det sku bli oss, Lenge Sia, Tender Falls the Rain, Trader Joe's, Please Don't Leave Me, Out of Here, Loneliness and Never Felt So Good (title track).
Full streaming links and track listings are on the Music page.

sections.title: Collaborations
paragraphs: Select recordings feature John Norum and Ronni Le Tekrø. Studio work is produced with Peter Michelsen at The Norwegian Sound in Mjøndalen — the same creative hub behind major Norwegian pop and rock productions.
Håvard maintains a long-standing connection to Europe through his cousin, guitarist John Norum.

sections.title: Side projects & live experience
paragraphs: Alongside his solo career Håvard has been part of Cinematic World, The Norwegian Beatles, and Three Men Electric Jam — gaining extensive experience on stages across Norway and internationally in Europe, the UK, and the United States.
Live concerts continue as Håvard Pedersen & The Blues Is Alright Band for full-band shows, alongside the current Håvard Pedersen Trio power trio format.

sections.title: Mezzabarba
paragraphs: Recognised and endorsed by Mezzabarba — premium amplification behind the live sound.

sections.title: Beyond the stage
paragraphs: Beyond the stage Håvard is a creative entrepreneur with a strong independent spirit: after years in the retail and business world he has chosen to focus on music and self-created projects — artistic freedom, live performance, and meaningful connection with audiences.
He has faced personal challenges, including health setbacks and major back surgery, and remains committed to persistence, reinvention, and music as both expression and purpose.

sections.title: Gretsch
paragraphs: Håvard Pedersen is an official Gretsch-endorsed artist — White Falcon, Electromatic and stage guitars are central to his visual and sonic identity.
sections.imageAlt: Håvard Pedersen with Gretsch White Falcon

sections.title: The Norwegian Sound
paragraphs: Recording sessions with producer Peter Michelsen at The Norwegian Sound continue Håvard's studio work — balancing live energy with crafted production for singles and upcoming album material.
